title: Asymptotically Good Quantum Locally Testable Codes
abstract: We construct explicit families of asymptotically good quantum locally testable codes over qubits. More precseily, we construct explicit quantum LDPC CSS codes over qubits having constant rate, constant relative distance and constant weight local testers with constant soundness.
summary: This paper presents a theoretical construction of quantum locally testable codes (qLTCs) over qubits. By utilizing advanced algebraic and combinatorial techniques, the authors achieve codes with optimal asymptotic parameters, including constant rate and distance. This is a significant theoretical advance for quantum error correction, enabling the design of robust quantum hardware protocols.
main_problem: The primary goal is to construct explicit families of asymptotically good quantum locally testable codes (qLTCs) over qubits.
main_result: The authors construct explicit quantum LDPC CSS codes that achieve constant rate, constant relative distance, constant weight local testers, and constant soundness.
method: The construction employs advanced algebraic and combinatorial tools, including cubical complexes, cosheaves, and product expansion, adapting abstract frameworks from coding theory and algebraic topology.
model_or_system: The model is quantum error-correcting codes, specifically focusing on quantum LDPC CSS codes over qubits. The testability relates to the expected fraction of violated checks, which controls the normalized distance from the codespace.
key_observables: Code parameters such as rate, relative distance, tester weight, and soundness constant are key observables. Syndrome weight and distance eigenvalues are also central.
important_parameters: The construction requires maintaining constant values for rate, relative distance, tester weight, and soundness, alongside managing complex algebraic parameters related to the underlying geometry.
main_assumptions: The work relies on deep mathematical machinery, including the properties of Ramanujan cubical complexes and the ability to reconcile their noncommuting labels with the required differential structure.
paper_structure: The paper follows a highly technical development path, moving from general preliminaries to complex constructions involving cubical complexes and cosheaves, culminating in the main theorems establishing the existence of the desired code family.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete constructions for quantum codes with desirable local testing properties, which is crucial for building fault-tolerant quantum computation protocols.
